preamble.title: Preamble: purposes of government
preamble.plain: Government exists to secure the body politic and let individuals enjoy their natural rights in safety; when it fails, the people have a right to alter it. The people of Massachusetts establish this Declaration of Rights and Frame of Government.
rights: the people have a right to alter the government
powers: do agree upon, ordain and establish the following Declaration of Rights, and Frame of Government

decl1.title: Natural rights of all people
decl1.plain: Annulled: This article said all men are born free and equal and have natural, essential and unalienable rights, including enjoying and defending their lives and liberties, acquiring and protecting property, and seeking safety and happiness. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CVI.
rights: the right of enjoying and defending their lives and liberties
that of acquiring, possessing, and protecting property
that of seeking and obtaining their safety and happiness

decl2.title: Freedom of worship
decl2.plain: Worshipping the Supreme Being publicly and at stated seasons is the right and duty of all men in society. No subject shall be hurt, molested or restrained for worshipping God as his conscience dictates, or for his religious profession or sentiments, if he does not disturb the public peace or others' worship.
rights: for worshipping God in the manner and season most agreeable to the dictates of his own conscience
for his religious profession or sentiments
limits: no subject shall be hurt, molested, or restrained, in his person, liberty, or estate

decl3.title: Public worship and religious teachers
decl3.plain: Annulled: A bracketed note says Article XI of the Amendments was substituted for this article. It provided that the legislature shall require towns, parishes and religious societies to provide for public worship and Protestant teachers, could enjoin attendance on their instruction, and that no sect shall be subordinated to another by law.

decl4.title: Right of self-government
decl4.plain: The people of the commonwealth have the sole and exclusive right to govern themselves as a free, sovereign and independent state, and keep every power, jurisdiction and right not expressly delegated by them to the United States of America in Congress assembled.
rights: the sole and exclusive right of governing themselves, as a free, sovereign, and independent state
exercise and enjoy every power, jurisdiction, and right

decl5.title: Officials accountable to the people
decl5.plain: All power resides originally in the people and is derived from them, so the magistrates and officers of government, whether legislative, executive or judicial, are their substitutes and agents and are at all times accountable to them.
powers: All power residing originally in the people

decl6.title: No hereditary privileges
decl6.plain: No man, corporation or association has any title to advantages or exclusive privileges apart from the community except from services rendered to the public. That title is not hereditary, so a man born a magistrate, lawgiver or judge is absurd and unnatural.
limits: have any other title to obtain advantages, or particular and exclusive privileges, distinct from those of the community
neither hereditary, nor transmissible to children, or descendants, or relations by blood

decl7.title: Purpose of government; right to change it
decl7.plain: Government is instituted for the common good and the protection, safety, prosperity and happiness of the people, not for the profit of any one man, family or class. The people alone have an unalienable right to institute government and to reform, alter or totally change it.
rights: an incontestable, unalienable, and indefeasible right to institute government
to reform, alter, or totally change the same
limits: not for the profit, honor, or private interest of any one man, family, or class of men

decl8.title: Right to remove officers by election
decl8.plain: To keep those in authority from becoming oppressors, the people have a right, at periods and in a manner set by their frame of government, to return public officers to private life and to fill vacancies by regular elections and appointments.
rights: to cause their public officers to return to private life
to fill up vacant places by certain and regular elections and appointments

decl9.title: Free elections and equal right to vote
decl9.plain: All elections ought to be free, and all inhabitants of the commonwealth who have the qualifications set by the frame of government have an equal right to elect officers and to be elected to public employments.
rights: an equal right to elect officers, and to be elected, for public employments

decl10.title: Protection of life, liberty and property
decl10.plain: Each individual has a right to be protected in life, liberty and property under standing laws, and must contribute his share to that protection. No property may be taken or applied to public uses without his consent or that of the representative body, and property appropriated to public uses requires reasonable compensation.
rights: a right to be protected by it in the enjoyment of his life, liberty and property
he shall receive a reasonable compensation therefor
limits: no part of the property of any individual can, with justice, be taken from him, or applied to public uses
are not controllable by any other laws

decl11.title: Right to a remedy in the laws
decl11.plain: Every subject ought to find a certain remedy in the laws for injuries to his person, property or character, and to obtain right and justice freely, completely, promptly and without delay, conformably to the laws.
rights: ought to find a certain remedy, by having recourse to the laws
obtain right and justice freely, and without being obliged to purchase it

decl12.title: Rights of the accused; trial by jury
decl12.plain: No subject shall answer for a crime until it is fully described to him, or be compelled to accuse himself. He may produce favorable proofs, meet witnesses face to face and be fully heard. No one may be deprived of life, liberty or property but by judgment of his peers or the law of the land.
rights: a right to produce all proofs, that may be favorable to him
to meet the witnesses against him face to face
to be fully heard in his defense by himself, or his council at his election
limits: No subject shall be held to answer for any crimes or offence
be compelled to accuse, or furnish evidence against himself
no subject shall be arrested, imprisoned, despoiled, or deprived of his property, immunities, or privileges
the legislature shall not make any law, that shall subject any person to a capital or infamous punishment

decl13.title: Facts tried in the vicinity
decl13.plain: In criminal prosecutions, verifying the facts in the vicinity where they happen is one of the greatest securities of the citizen's life, liberty and property.

decl14.title: Searches, seizures and warrants
decl14.plain: Every subject has a right to be secure from unreasonable searches and seizures. Warrants are contrary to this right unless supported by oath or affirmation and specially designating the persons or objects, and no warrant ought to be issued except in cases and with formalities the laws prescribe.
rights: a right to be secure from all unreasonable searches, and seizures, of his person, his houses, his papers, and all his possessions
limits: All warrants, therefore, are contrary to this right
no warrant ought to be issued

decl15.title: Right to a jury in civil cases
decl15.plain: In controversies about property and suits between persons, the parties have a right to a jury trial, which shall be held sacred, except where other practice was used before, and unless the legislature finds it necessary to alter it in high-seas and mariners' wages cases.
rights: the parties have a right to a trial by jury
limits: this method of procedure shall be held sacred

decl16.title: Liberty of the press
decl16.plain: Annulled: This article, printed in brackets as superseded, said the liberty of the press is essential to the security of freedom and ought not to be restrained in this commonwealth. A bracketed note in the text says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXVII.

decl17.title: Right to bear arms; civilian control of military
decl17.plain: The people have a right to keep and bear arms for the common defence. Because armies in peacetime are dangerous to liberty, they ought not to be maintained without the legislature's consent, and the military shall always be subordinate to and governed by the civil authority.
rights: The people have a right to keep and to bear arms for the common defence
limits: ought not to be maintained without the consent of the legislature
the military power shall always be held in an exact subordination to the civil authority

decl18.title: Adherence to fundamental principles
decl18.plain: Frequent recurrence to the constitution's fundamental principles and to piety, justice, moderation, temperance, industry and frugality is necessary to a free government. The people ought to heed these in choosing officers and have a right to require lawgivers and magistrates to observe them.
rights: a right to require of their lawgivers and magistrates, an exact and constant observance of them

decl19.title: Right to assemble, instruct and petition
decl19.plain: The people have a right, in an orderly and peaceable manner, to assemble to consult on the common good, to give instructions to their representatives, and to ask the legislative body, by addresses, petitions or remonstrances, for redress of wrongs and grievances.
rights: to assemble to consult upon the common good
give instructions to their representatives
to request of the legislative body, by the way of addresses, petitions, or remonstrances, redress of the wrongs done them

decl20.title: Only the legislature may suspend laws
decl20.plain: The power of suspending the laws, or their execution, ought never to be exercised except by the legislature or by authority derived from it, and only in the particular cases the legislature expressly provides for.
limits: ought never to be exercised but by the legislature, or by authority derived from it

decl21.title: Freedom of debate in the legislature
decl21.plain: The freedom of deliberation, speech and debate in either house of the legislature is so essential to the rights of the people that it cannot be the foundation of any accusation, prosecution, action or complaint in any other court or place.
rights: The freedom of deliberation, speech and debate, in either house of the legislature
limits: it cannot be the foundation of any accusation or prosecution, action or complaint, in any other court or place whatsoever

decl22.title: Frequent meetings of the legislature
decl22.plain: The legislature ought to assemble frequently to redress grievances, to correct, strengthen and confirm the laws, and to make new laws, as the common good may require.

decl23.title: No taxes without consent
decl23.plain: No subsidy, charge, tax, impost or duties ought to be established, fixed, laid or levied, under any pretext, without the consent of the people or their representatives in the legislature.
limits: No subsidy, charge, tax, impost, or duties, ought to be established, fixed, laid, or levied, under any pretext whatsoever

decl24.title: No ex post facto laws
decl24.plain: Laws that punish actions done before those laws existed, and that were not declared crimes by earlier laws, are unjust, oppressive and inconsistent with the fundamental principles of a free government.
limits: are unjust, oppressive, and inconsistent with the fundamental principles of a free government

decl25.title: No legislative convictions for treason or felony
decl25.plain: No subject ought, in any case or at any time, to be declared guilty of treason or felony by the legislature.
limits: No subject ought, in any case, or in any time, to be declared guilty of treason or felony by the legislature

decl26.title: No excessive bail or cruel punishment
decl26.plain: No magistrate or court of law shall demand excessive bail or sureties, impose excessive fines, or inflict cruel or unusual punishments.
limits: shall demand excessive bail or sureties
impose excessive fines
inflict cruel or unusual punishments

decl27.title: Quartering of soldiers
decl27.plain: In peacetime no soldier ought to be quartered in any house without the owner's consent. In wartime, quarters ought to be made only by the civil magistrate, in a manner ordained by the legislature.
limits: no soldier ought to be quartered in any house without the consent of the owner
such quarters ought not to be made but by the civil magistrate

decl28.title: Limits on martial law
decl28.plain: No person can be subject to law-martial, or to its penalties or pains, except those employed in the army or navy and the militia in actual service, unless by authority of the legislature.
limits: No person can in any case be subject to law-martial, or to any penalties or pains, by virtue of that law

decl29.title: Independent judges
decl29.plain: An impartial interpretation of the laws and administration of justice is essential to every individual's rights. Every citizen has a right to be tried by judges as free, impartial and independent as possible, so supreme judicial court judges should hold office during good behavior with honorable salaries set by standing laws.
rights: the right of every citizen to be tried by judges as free, impartial and independent as the lot of humanity will admit

decl30.title: Separation of powers
decl30.plain: The legislative, executive and judicial departments shall never exercise each other's powers, so that the commonwealth may be a government of laws and not of men.
limits: the legislative department shall never exercise the executive and judicial powers, or either of them
the executive shall never exercise the legislative and judicial powers, or either of them
the judicial shall never exercise the legislative and executive powers, or either of them

p2-c1-s1-a1.title: Two branches: the General Court
p2-c1-s1-a1.plain: The legislature has two branches, a Senate and House of Representatives, each with a negative on the other. It shall assemble every year and be styled The General Court of Massachusetts. Bracketed wording on the meeting and dissolving dates is printed as superseded.
powers: each of which shall have a negative on the other

p2-c1-s1-a2.title: Governor's approval and veto of bills
p2-c1-s1-a2.plain: No bill or resolve becomes law until laid before the governor. He signs it if he approves, or returns it with written objections. Two thirds of each house, voting by yeas and nays, may pass it anyway. A bracketed sentence on bills not returned within five days is printed as superseded.
powers: he shall return the same, together with his objections thereto, in writing
if approved by two thirds of the members present, shall have the force of a law
limits: No bill or resolve of the senate or house of representatives shall become a law

p2-c1-s1-a3.title: Power to create courts
p2-c1-s1-a3.plain: The general court has full power to set up courts of record and other courts, held in the commonwealth's name, to hear and decide all criminal and civil matters arising within it and to award execution. Those courts may administer oaths or affirmations.
powers: shall forever have full power and authority to erect and constitute judicatories and courts of record, or other courts
full power and authority, from time to time, to administer oaths or affirmations

p2-c1-s1-a4.title: Lawmaking and taxing powers of the general court
p2-c1-s1-a4.plain: The general court may make all wholesome and reasonable laws not contrary to this constitution for the commonwealth's good, provide for civil officers and set their duties, and levy reasonable taxes, duties and excises, spent by the governor's warrant with the council's consent. Estates are to be revalued at least every ten years.
powers: to make, ordain, and establish, all manner of wholesome and reasonable orders, laws, statutes, and ordinances
to name and settle annually, or provide by fixed laws, for the naming and settling all civil officers
to set forth the several duties, powers, and limits, of the several civil and military officers of this commonwealth
to impose and levy proportional and reasonable assessments, rates, and taxes
to impose and levy, reasonable duties and excises
limits: so as the same be not repugnant or contrary to this constitution

p2-c1-s2-a1.title: Senate districts and number of senators
p2-c1-s2-a1.plain: Superseded: It provided for forty councillors and senators elected yearly from districts set by the general court in proportion to public taxes paid, with the counties as districts until altered.

p2-c1-s2-a2.title: Election of senators at town meetings
p2-c1-s2-a2.plain: The senate is the first branch of the legislature. Senators are elected at town meetings called by the selectmen, who count the votes and send attested records to the secretary of the commonwealth. Voters in plantations and other places outside the towns may also vote. Bracketed dates and voter qualifications are printed as superseded.
rights: shall have the same privilege of voting for councillors and senators in the plantations where they reside
shall have the privilege of giving in their votes for councillors and senators in the town where they shall be assessed

p2-c1-s2-a3.title: Examining returns and summoning senators
p2-c1-s2-a3.plain: The governor with five of the council shall examine the returned copies of the election records and, fourteen days before the senate convenes, summon those who appear chosen to take their seats. For the first year the former president and council did this. Bracketed dates are printed as superseded.

p2-c1-s2-a4.title: Senate judges its own elections
p2-c1-s2-a4.plain: The senate is the final judge of the elections, returns and qualifications of its own members, and shall determine and declare who is elected by each district. The bracketed wording on dates, majority votes and filling vacancies is printed as superseded.
powers: The senate shall be the final judge of the elections, returns and qualifications of their own members

p2-c1-s2-a5.title: Qualifications of senators
p2-c1-s2-a5.plain: No person can be elected a senator who has not been an inhabitant of the commonwealth for the five years immediately before the election, and he must live in his district when elected. Bracketed property requirements are printed as superseded.
limits: no person shall be capable of being elected as a senator

p2.title: The people form the Commonwealth
p2.plain: The people living in the territory formerly called the Province of Massachusetts Bay agree with each other to form a free, sovereign and independent body politic, or state, named The Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

p2-c1-s2-a6.title: Senate may adjourn itself
p2-c1-s2-a6.plain: The senate has power to adjourn itself, but such adjournments may not exceed two days at a time.
powers: The senate shall have power to adjourn themselves
limits: provided such adjournments do not exceed two days at a time

p2-c1-s2-a7.title: Senate chooses its president and rules
p2-c1-s2-a7.plain: The senate chooses its own president, appoints its own officers and determines its own rules of proceedings.
powers: The senate shall choose its own president, appoint its own officers, and determine its own rules of proceedings

p2-c1-s2-a8.title: Senate tries impeachments
p2-c1-s2-a8.plain: The senate is a court to hear and determine impeachments made by the house against officers of the commonwealth for misconduct and mal-administration. Senators are sworn first. Judgment extends only to removal and disqualification from office; the person convicted may still be indicted, tried and punished under the laws.
powers: The senate shall be a court with full authority to hear and determine all impeachments made by the house of representatives
limits: Their judgment, however shall not extend further than to removal from office and disqualification to hold or enjoy any place of honor, trust, or profit, under this commonwealth

p2-c1-s2-a9.title: Senate quorum
p2-c1-s2-a9.plain: Superseded: It provided that not less than sixteen members of the senate would constitute a quorum for doing business.

p2-c1-s3-a1.title: Representation of the people
p2-c1-s3-a1.plain: The legislature shall include a representation of the people, elected and founded upon the principle of equality. The bracketed word "annually" is printed as superseded.

p2-c1-s3-a2.title: Town representatives and fines
p2-c1-s3-a2.plain: The house of representatives may fine towns that neglect to choose and return members. Bracketed paragraphs on how many representatives towns could elect by ratable polls, and on paying members' travel expenses, are printed as superseded.
powers: the house of representatives shall have power from time to time to impose fines upon such towns as shall neglect to choose and return members to the same

p2-c1-s3-a3.title: Choosing representatives by written votes
p2-c1-s3-a3.plain: Every member of the house of representatives shall be chosen by written votes. Bracketed residence and property qualifications for representatives are printed as superseded.

p2-c1-s3-a4.title: Who could vote for representatives
p2-c1-s3-a4.plain: Superseded: It gave every male person aged twenty-one, resident in a town for one year and holding a freehold of three pounds annual income or any estate worth sixty pounds, a right to vote for the town's representatives.

p2-c1-s3-a5.title: When representatives are chosen
p2-c1-s3-a5.plain: Superseded: It provided that members of the house of representatives would be chosen annually in May, at least ten days before the last Wednesday of that month.

p2-c1-s3-a6.title: House impeaches; senate tries
p2-c1-s3-a6.plain: The house of representatives is the grand inquest of the commonwealth, and all impeachments it makes shall be heard and tried by the senate.
powers: The house of representatives shall be the grand inquest of this commonwealth

p2-c1-s3-a7.title: Money bills start in the house
p2-c1-s3-a7.plain: All money bills must originate in the house of representatives, but the senate may propose or concur with amendments as on other bills.
powers: the senate may propose or concur with amendments

p2-c1-s3-a8.title: House may adjourn itself
p2-c1-s3-a8.plain: The house of representatives has power to adjourn itself, but such adjournment may not exceed two days at a time.
powers: The house of representatives shall have power to adjourn themselves
limits: provided such adjournment shall not exceed two days at a time

p2-c1-s3-a9.title: House quorum
p2-c1-s3-a9.plain: Superseded: It provided that not less than sixty members of the house of representatives would constitute a quorum for doing business.

p2-c1-s3-a10.title: House powers, contempt and member privilege
p2-c1-s3-a10.plain: The house judges its members' elections and qualifications, chooses its speaker and officers, and sets its rules. It may imprison non-members for disrespect, threats, assaults on members or witnesses, or rescuing persons it arrested. Members may not be arrested or held to bail on mesne process while going to, returning from or attending the general assembly.
rights: no member of the house of representatives shall be arrested, or held to bail on mesne process
powers: shall be the judge of the returns, elections, and qualifications of its own members
shall choose their own speaker
They shall have authority to punish by imprisonment

p2-c1-s3-a11.title: Senate and governor may punish contempt
p2-c1-s3-a11.plain: The senate has the same powers in like cases, and the governor and council the same authority to punish. No such imprisonment may exceed thirty days. Each house may try cases concerning its rights and privileges by committees or as it thinks best.
powers: The senate shall have the same powers in the like cases
the governor and council shall have the same authority to punish in like cases
the senate and house of representatives may try, and determine, all cases where their rights and privileges are concerned
limits: no imprisonment on the warrant or order of the governor, council, senate, or house of representatives, for either of the above described offences, be for a term exceeding thirty days

p2-c2-s1-a1.title: The Governor
p2-c2-s1-a1.plain: There shall be a supreme executive magistrate styled The Governor of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, whose title shall be His Excellency.

p2-c2-s1-a2.title: Choosing the governor; qualifications
p2-c2-s1-a2.plain: The governor shall be chosen, and no person is eligible unless he has been an inhabitant of the commonwealth for the seven years before his election. Bracketed wording on annual election, property and religion requirements is printed as superseded.
limits: no person shall be eligible to this office

p2-c2-s1-a3.title: How the governor is elected
p2-c2-s1-a3.plain: Voters for senators and representatives vote for governor at town meetings; the town clerk and selectmen count, record and send sealed lists to the secretary, who lays them before the legislature. If no one wins, the house picks two of the top four and the senate elects one. Bracketed dates and "majority" are printed as superseded.

p2-c2-s1-a4.title: Governor and council
p2-c2-s1-a4.plain: The governor may at his discretion assemble the councillors. The governor with the councillors, or at least five of them, shall hold a council to order and direct the affairs of the commonwealth under the constitution and the laws.
powers: The governor shall have authority from time to time, at his discretion, to assemble and call together the councillors of this commonwealth
for the ordering and directing the affairs of the commonwealth

p2-c2-s1-a5.title: Governor may adjourn or prorogue the general court
p2-c2-s1-a5.plain: The governor, with advice of council, may adjourn or prorogue the general court as the two houses desire, prorogue it in recess up to ninety days, call it together sooner, and move the session elsewhere in case of infectious distemper or danger. Bracketed wording on dissolving the court in May is printed as superseded.
powers: shall have full power and authority, during the session of the general court to adjourn or prorogue the same
to call it together sooner than the time to which it may be adjourned or prorogued
he may direct the session to be held at some other, the most convenient place within the state
limits: not exceeding ninety days in any one recess

p2-c2-s1-a6.title: Governor settles adjournment disagreements
p2-c2-s1-a6.plain: When the two houses disagree about the necessity, expediency or time of adjournment or prorogation, the governor, with the advice of the council, may adjourn or prorogue the general court for up to ninety days, as the public good requires.
powers: shall have a right to adjourn or prorogue the general court
limits: not exceeding ninety days

p2-c2-s1-a7.title: Governor as commander in chief
p2-c2-s1-a7.plain: Annulled: This article made the governor commander in chief of all military forces of the state, with power to train and govern the militia and defend the commonwealth, but barred him from marching inhabitants out of the state without their consent or the general court's. A note says Amendments, Art. LIV annulled and superseded it.

p2-c2-s1-a8.title: Governor's pardoning power
p2-c2-s1-a8.plain: Annulled: This article gave the governor, with the advice of council, the power of pardoning offences, except convictions by the senate on impeachment, and said no pardon granted before conviction would avail the party pleading it. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXIII.

p2-c2-s1-a9.title: Governor appoints judicial officers
p2-c2-s1-a9.plain: All judicial officers, the solicitor-general and coroners shall be nominated and appointed by the governor, with the advice and consent of the council, and each nomination must be made at least seven days before the appointment. Bracketed offices (attorney-general, sheriffs, registers of probate) are printed as superseded.
powers: shall be nominated and appointed by the governor, by and with the advice and consent of the council

p2-c2-s1-a10.title: Election and appointment of militia officers
p2-c2-s1-a10.plain: Annulled: This article provided for electing militia captains, subalterns, field officers and brigadiers by written votes, appointment of major-generals by the two houses, commissioning by the governor, removal of officers only by address of both houses or court-martial, and other militia appointments and divisions. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

p2-c2-s1-a11.title: Treasury money only by governor's warrant
p2-c2-s1-a11.plain: No money may be issued out of the treasury except by warrant of the governor, with the advice and consent of the council, for the defence and support of the commonwealth and protection of its inhabitants, agreeably to acts of the general court. Sums for redeeming bills of credit or treasurer's notes, or paying their interest, are excepted.
powers: by warrant under the hand of the governor for the time being, with the advice and consent of the council
limits: No moneys shall be issued out of the treasury of this commonwealth, and disposed of

p2-c2-s1-a12.title: Reports of public property to the governor
p2-c2-s1-a12.plain: Public boards, superintending officers of public magazines and stores, and commanding officers of forts and garrisons must account to the governor every three months, and when required, for all public property in their care, and give him plans of forts. Boards and public officers must pass on public letters and despatches. The bracketed "commissary-general" is printed as superseded.

p2-c2-s1-a13.title: Salaries of the governor and justices
p2-c2-s1-a13.plain: So the governor is not dependent on members of the general court, he shall have an honorable stated salary of fixed and permanent value, established by standing laws. Permanent and honorable salaries shall also be established by law for justices of the supreme judicial court, and enlarged if found insufficient.

p2-c2-s2-a1.title: Election of the lieutenant governor
p2-c2-s2-a1.plain: There shall be an elected lieutenant governor, titled His Honor, qualified in residence like the governor and elected on the same day, in the same manner and by the same electors. If no one is chosen, the senate and house fill the vacancy as for governor. Bracketed words (annually, religion, property, a majority) are printed as superseded.

p2-c2-s2-a2.title: Governor presides over the council
p2-c2-s2-a2.plain: The governor, or in his absence the lieutenant governor, is president of the council but has no vote in council. The lieutenant governor is always a member of the council except when the governor's chair is vacant.
limits: shall have no vote in council

p2-c2-s3-a1.title: The governor's council
p2-c2-s3-a1.plain: There shall be a council to advise the governor in the executive part of government, which the governor may assemble at his discretion. The governor, with at least five councillors, may hold a council to order and direct the commonwealth's affairs according to law. The bracketed number "nine" is printed as superseded.
powers: shall have full power and authority, from time to time, at his discretion, to assemble and call together

p2-c2-s3-a2.title: Choosing councillors
p2-c2-s3-a2.plain: Annulled: This article provided that nine councillors be chosen annually by joint ballot of the senators and representatives from those returned as councillors and senators, with any shortfall made up from the people at large, and senators chosen vacating their senate seats. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art. XVI.

p2-c2-s3-a3.title: Rank of councillors
p2-c2-s3-a3.plain: The councillors, in the civil arrangements of the commonwealth, rank next after the lieutenant governor.

p2-c2-s3-a4.title: Councillors per district
p2-c2-s3-a4.plain: Annulled: This article provided that not more than two councillors be chosen out of any one district. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art XVI.

p2-c2-s3-a5.title: Council records and dissents
p2-c2-s3-a5.plain: The council's resolutions and advice shall be recorded in a register and signed by the members present. Either house of the legislature may call for this record at any time, and any councillor may insert his opinion contrary to the majority's resolution.
rights: any member of the council may insert his opinion, contrary to the resolution of the majority
powers: this record may be called for at any time by either house of the legislature

p2-c2-s3-a6.title: Council acts when both offices are vacant
p2-c2-s3-a6.plain: Annulled: This article provided that when the offices of governor and lieutenant governor were both vacant, the council, or most of them, would have full power to do whatever the governor or lieutenant governor could do. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LV.

p2-c2-s3-a7.title: Order of legislative elections
p2-c2-s3-a7.plain: Annulled: This article let the May elections by the two houses be adjourned day to day until completed, and set their order: senate vacancies first, then governor and lieutenant governor if the people made no choice, then the council. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Arts. XVI and XXV.

p2-c2-s4-a1.title: Choosing secretary, treasurer and other officers
p2-c2-s4-a1.plain: Superseded: It provided that the secretary, treasurer and receiver-general, commissary-general, notaries public and naval officers be chosen annually by joint ballot of the senators and representatives, and that no man be eligible as treasurer and receiver-general more than five years successively.

p2-c2-s4-a2.title: Secretary keeps the records
p2-c2-s4-a2.plain: The commonwealth's records shall be kept in the secretary's office. The secretary may appoint deputies, for whose conduct he is accountable, and shall attend the governor and council, the senate and the house, in person or by deputies, as they require.
powers: who may appoint his deputies

p2-c3-a1.title: Tenure and removal of judicial officers
p2-c3-a1.plain: Annulled: This article required each commission officer's tenure to be expressed in his commission, and let judicial officers hold office during good behavior, though the governor, with consent of the council, could remove them upon the address of both houses. A note says Amendments, Art. XCVIII annulled it.

p2-c3-a2.title: Opinions of the justices
p2-c3-a2.plain: Annulled: This article gave each branch of the legislature, and the governor and council, authority to require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court upon important questions of law and upon solemn occasions. A note says Amendments, Art. LXXXV amended and superseded it.

p2-c3-a3.title: Seven-year commissions for justices of the peace
p2-c3-a3.plain: So the people do not suffer from justices of the peace who fail in their duties staying long in place, all their commissions expire and become void seven years from their dates; an expired commission may be renewed, or another person appointed, as best serves the commonwealth.
limits: all commissions of justices of the peace shall expire and become void, in the term of seven years from their respective dates

p2-c3-a4.title: Times and places of probate courts
p2-c3-a4.plain: Judges of probate shall hold their courts at places and on fixed days as the people's convenience requires, and the legislature shall appoint those times and places; until it does, the courts are held where and when the judges direct.
powers: the legislature shall, from time to time, hereafter appoint such times and places

p2-c3-a5.title: Marriage, divorce and probate appeals
p2-c3-a5.plain: All causes of marriage, divorce and alimony, and all appeals from the judges of probate, shall be heard and determined by the governor and council until the legislature, by law, makes other provision.
powers: shall be heard and determined by the governor and council

p2-c4.title: Delegates to Congress
p2-c4.plain: Annulled: This chapter had the senate and house, by joint ballot in one room, elect the commonwealth's delegates to the congress of the United States each June for one-year terms, subject to recall. A note says the adoption of the Constitution of the United States annulled it.

p2-c5-s1-a1.title: Rights of Harvard College confirmed
p2-c5-s1-a1.plain: Citing Harvard College's founding and the value of arts, sciences and literature, it declares that the President and Fellows of Harvard College, their successors, officers and servants keep all their existing powers, rights, privileges, immunities and franchises, ratified and confirmed forever.
rights: all the powers, authorities, rights, liberties, privileges, immunities and franchises, which they now have or are entitled to have

p2-c5-s1-a2.title: Gifts to Harvard College confirmed
p2-c5-s1-a2.plain: All past gifts, grants, devises, legacies and conveyances made to Harvard College, or to its president and fellows under any description, are forever confirmed to the president and fellows and their successors, according to the true intent of the donors, grantors and devisors.
rights: are hereby forever confirmed unto the president and fellows of Harvard College

p2-c5-s1-a3.title: Legislature may alter Harvard's government
p2-c5-s1-a3.plain: Nothing prevents the legislature from making alterations in the government of the university at Cambridge that are conducive to its advantage and the interest of the republic of letters. Bracketed wording naming the overseers of Harvard College is printed as superseded.
powers: making such alterations in the government of the said university

p2-c5-s2.title: Duty to cherish literature and sciences
p2-c5-s2.plain: Because wisdom, knowledge and virtue spread among the people preserve their rights and liberties, legislatures and magistrates must cherish literature, the sciences and schools, especially the university at Cambridge, encourage institutions promoting agriculture, arts, sciences and commerce, and inculcate humanity, charity, industry and honesty.

p2-c6-a1.title: Oaths of office
p2-c6-a1.plain: Every person chosen governor, lieutenant governor, councillor, senator or representative, and every appointed judicial, executive, military or other officer, must take and subscribe an oath or affirmation to faithfully discharge the office's duties. Quakers may affirm instead. Bracketed declarations and oaths are printed as superseded.

p2-c6-a2.title: Offices that cannot be held together
p2-c6-a2.plain: The governor, lieutenant governor and supreme judicial court judges may hold no other office or take pay from another government; no one may hold more than one of certain offices or more than two appointed or elected offices; listed officers cannot sit in the legislature; those convicted of election bribery are barred.
limits: shall hold any other office or place, under the authority of this commonwealth
nor shall they hold any other place or office, or receive any pension or salary from any other state or government or power whatever
No person shall be capable of holding or exercising at the same time, within this state more than one of the following offices
shall at the same time have a seat in the senate or house of representatives
no person shall ever be admitted to hold a seat in the legislature, or any office of trust or importance under the government of this commonwealth

p2-c6-a3.title: Value of money and property qualifications
p2-c6-a3.plain: Superseded: It provided that sums of money mentioned in the constitution be computed in silver at six shillings and eight pence per ounce, and gave the legislature power to increase property qualifications for persons elected to office.

p2-c6-a4.title: Form of commissions
p2-c6-a4.plain: All commissions shall be in the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, signed by the governor, attested by the secretary or his deputy, and have the great seal of the commonwealth affixed.

p2-c6-a5.title: Form of writs
p2-c6-a5.plain: All writs from the clerk's office of any court of law shall be in the name of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, under the seal of the issuing court, bear test of the first justice of the returnable court who is not a party, and be signed by its clerk.

p2-c6-a6.title: Earlier laws remain in force
p2-c6-a6.plain: Laws adopted, used and approved in the Province, Colony or State of Massachusetts Bay and practiced in the courts remain in full force until altered or repealed by the legislature, except parts repugnant to the rights and liberties in this constitution.
powers: altered or repealed by the legislature

p2-c6-a7.title: Writ of habeas corpus
p2-c6-a7.plain: The privilege and benefit of the writ of habeas corpus shall be enjoyed in the most free, easy, cheap, expeditious and ample manner, and the legislature may not suspend it except on the most urgent and pressing occasions, for no more than twelve months.
rights: The privilege and benefit of the writ of habeas corpus
limits: shall not be suspended by the legislature

p2-c6-a8.title: Enacting style of laws
p2-c6-a8.plain: All acts, statutes and laws must use the enacting style: "Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, and by the authority of the same."

p2-c6-a9.title: Officers continue until replaced
p2-c6-a9.plain: Superseded: It provided that, when this constitution took effect, existing civil and military officers, courts and executive and legislative bodies would keep their powers and continue their business until replacements were appointed and the general court and officers under this constitution were invested with their powers.

p2-c6-a10.title: Revising the constitution in 1795
p2-c6-a10.plain: Annulled: This article had the general court of 1795 direct towns and plantations to poll qualified voters on revising the constitution, and, if two thirds favored it, issue precepts for electing delegates to a convention, chosen like representatives. A note says Amendments, Art. XLVIII annulled it.

p2-c6-a11.title: Enrolling and printing the constitution
p2-c6-a11.plain: This form of government shall be enrolled on parchment, deposited in the secretary's office and be part of the laws of the land, and printed copies shall be prefixed to all future editions of the commonwealth's laws.

amend1.title: Bills not returned when the general court adjourns
amend1.plain: Annulled: It provided that if the general court adjourned within five days after a bill or resolve was laid before the governor, preventing its return with objections, the bill or resolve would not become a law. A note says Amendments, Art. XC, Sec. 2 superseded it.

amend2.title: City governments
amend2.plain: Annulled: It gave the general court power to erect city governments in towns, only in towns of at least twelve thousand inhabitants and with the consent of a majority of the inhabitants, with their by-laws subject to annulment by the general court. A note says Amendments, Art. LXXXIX annulled it.

amend3.title: Who may vote for state officers
amend3.plain: Every citizen who has resided six calendar months in the town or district where he claims a right to vote has a right to vote for governor, lieutenant governor, senators and representatives, except persons under guardianship; no other person may vote. Bracketed qualifications are printed as superseded.
rights: shall have a right to vote in such election of governor, lieutenant governor, senators and representatives
limits: no other person shall be entitled to vote in such election

amend4.title: Notaries public and other appointments
amend4.plain: Notaries public shall be appointed by the governor like judicial officers and hold office for seven years unless sooner removed. Bracketed paragraphs on vacancies for secretary or treasurer, a commissary-general and militia officers are printed as superseded and annulled.
powers: Notaries public shall be appointed by the governor

amend5.title: Militia companies vote for their officers
amend5.plain: Annulled: It gave all members of militia companies, whether under or above twenty-one years of age, a right to vote in elections of their captains and subalterns. A note says Amendments, Art. LIII annulled it.

amend6.title: Oath of allegiance for officers
amend6.plain: Every person chosen or appointed to any civil or military office must, before entering on its duties, swear to bear true faith and allegiance to the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and support its constitution. Quakers who decline the oath shall affirm instead.

amend7.title: No other oaths for elected officers
amend7.plain: No oath, declaration or subscription, except the oath in the preceding article and the oath of office, shall be required of the governor, lieutenant governor, councillors, senators or representatives to qualify them for their offices.
limits: No oath, declaration or subscription

amend8.title: Offices that cannot be held together
amend8.plain: Judges (except of the court of sessions) and federal officeholders (except postmasters) cannot also be governor, lieutenant governor, councillor or legislator; listed state officers who accept election to Congress resign their offices; and judges of the courts of common pleas hold no other state office.
limits: shall, at the same time, hold the office of governor, lieutenant governor, or councillor, or have a seat in the senate or house of representatives of this commonwealth
shall continue to hold his said office after being elected a member of Congress of the United States, and accepting that trust
shall hold no other office under the government of this commonwealth

amend9.title: Amending the constitution through the general court
amend9.plain: Annulled: It let amendments agreed to by a majority of senators and two thirds of representatives in two successive general courts be submitted to the people, becoming part of the constitution if ratified by a majority of qualified voters voting. A note says Amendments, Art. XLVIII annulled it.

amend10.title: Start of the political year
amend10.plain: The political year begins on the first Wednesday of January; the general court assembles every year that day and is dissolved the day before, but may assemble at other times or when called by the governor. Provisions referring to the last Wednesday of May now refer to January. Bracketed wording is printed as superseded.

amend11.title: Religious societies and equal protection of sects
amend11.plain: Replacing the third article of the bill of rights, religious societies have the right to elect and support their pastors and raise money for worship; members may leave by written notice; all peaceable sects are equally protected by law, and none may be subordinated to another.
rights: shall ever have the right to elect their pastors or religious teachers, to contract with them for their support, to raise money for erecting and repairing houses for public worship, for the maintenance of religious instruction, and for the payment of necessary expenses
shall be equally under the protection of the law
limits: no subordination of any one sect or denomination to another shall ever be established by law

amend12.title: Representation based on ratable polls
amend12.plain: Annulled: It provided a decennial census of ratable polls from 1837, gave towns representatives by numbers of polls, let small towns elect one in some years, let towns form representative districts, and had the governor and council fix the numbers. A note says later amendments superseded it.

amend13.title: Census, apportionment and no property qualification
amend13.plain: No possession of a freehold or other estate shall be required to hold a seat in either branch of the general court or in the executive council. Bracketed paragraphs on a decennial census, senators, representatives and councillors are printed as superseded.
limits: No possession of a freehold or of any other estate shall be required as a qualification

amend14.title: Highest number of votes wins
amend14.plain: In all elections of civil officers by the people that the constitution provides for, the person having the highest number of votes shall be deemed and declared elected.

amend15.title: Day of the state election
amend15.plain: Superseded: It provided that the meeting to choose the governor, lieutenant-governor, senators and representatives be held annually on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November, with a second meeting on the fourth Monday of November if representatives were not elected.

amend16.title: Election of councillors by districts
amend16.plain: Eight councillors shall be chosen annually by voters qualified to vote for governor, one from each of eight districts the legislature draws after each census. Councillors must have lived in the commonwealth five years. The governor and councillors examine election returns. Bracketed wording on vacancies is printed as superseded.
limits: No person shall be eligible to the office of councillor

amend17.title: Election of secretary, treasurer, auditor, attorney-general
amend17.plain: The secretary, treasurer and receiver-general, auditor and attorney-general shall be chosen on the November day for choosing the governor, with failures and session vacancies filled by joint ballot of the legislature and other vacancies by the governor's appointment. Each must have lived here five years. Bracketed wording is printed as superseded.
limits: No person shall be eligible to either of said offices

amend18.title: School money only for public schools
amend18.plain: Annulled: It required school moneys raised by towns and cities or appropriated by the state to be spent only on schools conducted under the town or city authorities, and never appropriated to any religious sect for its own schools. A note says later amendments superseded it.

amend19.title: Election of county officers and district-attorneys
amend19.plain: The legislature shall provide by general law for the people of the counties to elect sheriffs, registers of probate and clerks of the courts, and for the people of the districts to choose district-attorneys, for terms the legislature prescribes. Bracketed wording is printed as superseded.

amend20.title: Reading and writing test for office
amend20.plain: No person shall be eligible to office who cannot read the constitution in English and write his name, except persons with a physical disability, persons then entitled to vote, and persons then sixty or older. Bracketed wording on voting is printed as superseded.
limits: be eligible to office under the constitution of this commonwealth, who shall not be able to read the constitution in the English language, and write his name

amend21.title: Census and apportionment of representatives
amend21.plain: Annulled: It provided a census of legal voters, a house of two hundred and forty members apportioned to counties by legal voters, county boards dividing counties into representative districts, residence rules for representatives, and a quorum of one hundred members. A note says later amendments annulled and superseded it.

amend22.title: Census and senate districts
amend22.plain: Annulled: It provided a census of legal voters to apportion senators, a senate of forty members elected from forty districts of adjacent territory drawn by the general court, residence rules for senators, and a quorum of sixteen senators. A note says later amendments annulled and superseded it.

amend23.title: Waiting period for naturalized voters
amend23.plain: Annulled: It provided that no person of foreign birth could vote or hold office unless he had resided within the United States for two years after naturalization, without affecting rights already held or children of citizens born abroad. A note says Amendments, Art. XXVI annulled it.

amend24.title: Filling senate vacancies
amend24.plain: Any vacancy in the senate shall be filled by election by the people of the unrepresented district, upon the order of a majority of senators elected.

amend25.title: Filling council vacancies
amend25.plain: A vacancy in the council is filled by concurrent vote of the senate and house choosing an eligible person from the district; if the legislature is not in session, the governor, with the advice and consent of the council, may fill it by appointment.
powers: the senate and house of representatives shall, by concurrent vote, choose some eligible person
may fill the same by appointment of some eligible person

amend26.title: Annulling Article XXIII
amend26.plain: The twenty-third article of amendment, which barred persons of foreign birth from voting or holding office until two years after naturalization, is hereby wholly annulled.

amend27.title: Harvard College officers
amend27.plain: So much of article two of chapter six of the constitution as relates to persons holding the office of president, professor or instructor of Harvard College is hereby annulled.

amend28.title: Voting by honorably discharged veterans
amend28.plain: A person who served in the army or navy of the United States in time of war and was honorably discharged, if otherwise qualified to vote, shall not be disqualified because of the non-payment of a poll tax. Bracketed wording on paupers is printed as superseded.
limits: shall be disqualified therefor on account of

amend29.title: More than one polling place in towns
amend29.plain: The general court has full power to provide towns more than one place of public meeting for electing officers under the constitution and to prescribe how such meetings are called, held and conducted. Inconsistent provisions of the existing constitution are annulled.
powers: The general court shall have full power and authority to provide for the inhabitants of the towns in this commonwealth more than one place of public meeting

amend30.title: Voting after moving within the commonwealth
amend30.plain: A person otherwise qualified to vote for governor, lieutenant-governor, senators and representatives shall not, because of a change of residence within the commonwealth, be disqualified from voting for them in the city or town he left until six calendar months after moving.
limits: be disqualified from voting for said officers in the city or town from which he has removed his residence

amend31.title: Amending Article XXVIII on veterans' voting
amend31.plain: Superseded: It amended article twenty-eight by striking out "being a pauper" and inserting "receiving or having received aid from any city or town", and by striking out "if a pauper". The whole text is printed in brackets.

amend32.title: Removing the tax-paying voter qualification
amend32.plain: So much of article three of the amendments as required voters to have paid, by themselves or a parent, master or guardian, a state or county tax assessed within two years, and as covered citizens exempted from taxation, is hereby annulled.

amend33.title: Quorum of the general court
amend33.plain: A majority of the members of each branch of the general court is a quorum for business, but a smaller number may adjourn from day to day and compel the attendance of absent members. Inconsistent provisions of the existing constitution are annulled.
powers: a less number may adjourn from day to day, and compel the attendance of absent members

amend34.title: Removing the governor's property qualification
amend34.plain: So much of article two of section one of chapter two of part the second as required the governor to be seised in his own right of a freehold within the commonwealth worth one thousand pounds is hereby annulled.

amend35.title: Ending travel expense payments to representatives
amend35.plain: So much of article two of section three of chapter one as provided that the government pay members their expenses of travelling to the general assembly and returning home once each session is hereby annulled.

amend36.title: Removing commissioners of insolvency
amend36.plain: So much of article nineteen of the articles of amendment as is contained in the words "commissioners of insolvency" is hereby annulled.

amend37.title: Removing justices of the peace and notaries
amend37.plain: The governor, with the consent of the council, may remove justices of the peace and notaries public.
powers: may remove justices of the peace and notaries public

amend38.title: Voting machines and secret voting
amend38.plain: Voting machines or other mechanical devices for voting may be used at all elections under regulations prescribed by law, provided that the right of secret voting is preserved.
rights: the right of secret voting
powers: Voting machines or other mechanical devices for voting may be used at all elections

amend39.title: Taking extra land for highways
amend39.plain: Adding to article ten of part one, the legislature may by special acts authorize taking more land than needed for highways or streets, limited to land specified in the act and sufficient for building lots on both sides, and may authorize selling the remainder.
powers: The legislature may by special acts
may authorize the sale of the remainder for value

amend40.title: Disqualifying voters for corrupt election practices
amend40.plain: Article three of the amendments is amended by inserting after the word "guardianship" the words "and persons temporarily or permanently disqualified by law because of corrupt practices in respect to elections."

amend41.title: Taxing wild or forest lands
amend41.plain: Annulled: It gave the general court full power and authority to prescribe for wild or forest lands such methods of taxation as will develop and conserve the forest resources of the commonwealth. A note says Amendments, Art. CX annulled it.

amend42.title: Referring acts of the general court to the people
amend42.plain: Annulled: It gave the general court power to refer any act or resolve to the people by a majority yea and nay vote of each house; the act became law if approved by a majority of voters at the next regular state election. A note says it was annulled and superseded.

amend43.title: Taking land to relieve congestion and provide homes
amend43.plain: The general court may authorize the commonwealth to take land and to hold, improve, sub-divide, build upon and sell it to relieve congestion of population and provide homes for citizens, but not to sell such land or buildings at less than cost.
powers: The general court shall have power to authorize the commonwealth to take land
limits: shall not be deemed to authorize the sale of such land or buildings at less than the cost thereof

amend44.title: Income tax
amend44.plain: The general court may impose and levy a tax on income, at different rates for income from different classes of property but at a uniform rate throughout the commonwealth for the same class. It may tax income not derived from property at a lower rate and grant reasonable exemptions and abatements.
powers: to impose and levy a tax on income
may grant reasonable exemptions and abatements
limits: shall be levied at a uniform rate throughout the commonwealth upon incomes derived from the same class of property

amend45.title: Absent voting
amend45.plain: Annulled: It gave the general court power to provide by law for voting by qualified voters who, at the time of an election, are absent from the city or town of which they are inhabitants. A note says it was annulled and superseded.

amend46.title: Free exercise of religion and public money
amend46.plain: No law shall prohibit the free exercise of religion. Public school money goes only to schools conducted according to law, and public money or credit may not aid private or denominational schools and institutions or any church, with listed exceptions. Inmates keep religious exercises and cannot be compelled to attend religious services.
rights: the free exercise of religion
the opportunity of religious exercises therein of his own faith
limits: No law shall be passed prohibiting
shall be applied to, and expended in, no other schools than those which are conducted according to law
no grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of public credit shall be made or authorized by the commonwealth or any political division thereof
no inmate of such institution shall be compelled to attend religious services or receive religious instruction against his will

amend47.title: Food, necessaries and shelter in emergencies
amend47.plain: Maintaining and distributing at reasonable rates, during war, public exigency, emergency or distress, a sufficient supply of food and other common necessaries of life, and providing shelter, are public functions; the commonwealth and its cities and towns may take and provide them as the general court determines.
powers: the commonwealth and the cities and towns therein may take and may provide the same for their inhabitants

amend48-defi1.title: Initiative and referendum reserved to the people
amend48-defi1.plain: Legislative power stays vested in the general court, but the people reserve the popular initiative, the power of a specified number of voters to submit constitutional amendments and laws to the people, and the popular referendum, the power to submit laws enacted by the general court to the people.
powers: Legislative power shall continue to be vested in the general court
the people reserve to themselves the popular initiative
the popular referendum

amend48-init-initpeti2.title: What initiative petitions may contain
amend48-init-initpeti2.plain: An initiative petition must set out the full text of the measure. Measures on religion, judges, courts, local matters or specific appropriations, and propositions inconsistent with listed individual rights, may not be proposed by initiative. Petitions go to the general court. Bracketed Section 3, on originating petitions, is printed as superseded.
rights: The right to receive compensation for private property appropriated to public use
the right of access to and protection in courts of justice
the right of trial by jury
freedom of the press
freedom of speech
freedom of elections
the right of peaceable assembly
limits: shall be proposed by an initiative petition
shall be the subject of an initiative amendment
shall be the subject of an initiative or referendum petition
shall be the subject of an initiative petition
shall extend to the legislative power of the people

amend48-init-legiactigene3.title: Committee hearings and legislative substitutes
amend48-init-legiactigene3.plain: A measure introduced by initiative petition shall be referred to a committee, which hears the petitioners and parties in interest and reports in writing with reasons. The general court may submit to the people a legislative substitute, grouped on the ballot as an alternative.
powers: submit to the people a substitute for any measure introduced by initiative petition

amend48-init-legiaction4.title: Legislative action on proposed constitutional amendments
amend48-init-legiaction4.plain: An initiative amendment is voted on as introduced unless amended by three-fourths in joint session. A legislative amendment needs a majority of all members elected, and an initiative amendment one-fourth, in two successive general courts; then the people vote. Bracketed Sections 1 and 2 are printed as superseded.

amend48-init-legiaction5.title: Legislative action on proposed initiative laws
amend48-init-legiaction5.plain: Annulled: It required both houses to vote by June on an initiative law signed by twenty thousand voters; if not enacted and five thousand more signatures were filed, the people voted on it. A majority of the first ten signers could amend it. Notes in the text say both sections were superseded.

amend48-init-confandalte6.title: Conflicting and alternative measures
amend48-init-confandalte6.plain: When measures approved at the same election conflict, the one with the most affirmative votes governs, and a constitutional amendment governs a law. The general court may group measures on the ballot as conflicting or alternative, but not an amendment with a law.
powers: may provide for grouping and designating upon the ballot as conflicting measures or as alternative measures
limits: a proposed constitutional amendment and a proposed law shall not be so grouped

amend48-ref-whenstatshal1.title: When laws take effect
amend48-ref-whenstatshal1.plain: No law passed by the general court shall take effect earlier than ninety days after it has become a law, except emergency laws and laws which may not be made the subject of a referendum petition.
limits: No law passed by the general court shall take effect earlier than ninety days after it has become a law

amend48-ref-emermeas2.title: Emergency laws
amend48-ref-emermeas2.plain: An emergency law must contain a preamble stating the facts and that it is necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health, safety or convenience. The governor may file a statement making a law take effect forthwith. Franchise grants cannot be emergency laws. Bracketed wording on a two-thirds vote is printed as superseded.
powers: files with the secretary of the commonwealth a statement declaring
limits: no grant of any franchise or amendment thereof, or renewal or extension thereof for more than one year shall be declared to be an emergency law

amend48-ref-refepeti3.title: Referendum petitions
amend48-ref-refepeti3.plain: A referendum petition may ask for a referendum on any law not expressly excluded; laws on religion, judges, courts, local matters or ordinary appropriations are excluded. Petitions to suspend a law, or to repeal an emergency or unsuspended law, need ten signers and filing within thirty days. Bracketed wording is printed as superseded.
powers: A referendum petition may ask for a referendum to the people upon any law enacted by the general court
A referendum petition may ask for the repeal of an emergency law
limits: shall be the subject of a referendum petition

amend48-gen-idenandcert1.title: Identifying signatures and paid petition circulators
amend48-gen-idenandcert1.plain: Provision shall be made by law for identifying and certifying petition signatures and for penalties for signing or refusing to sign for money and for forgery. The general court may bar co-partnerships or corporations from circulating petitions for hire, license paid circulators, and make other reasonable regulations.
powers: may require individuals who circulate petitions for hire or reward to be licensed
may make other reasonable regulations to prevent abuses arising from the circulation of petitions for hire or reward

amend48-gen-limionsign2.title: Limit on signatures from one county
amend48-gen-limionsign2.plain: Not more than one-fourth of the certified signatures on any petition shall be those of registered voters of any one county.
limits: Not more than one-fourth of the certified signatures on any petition shall be those of registered voters of any one county

amend48-gen-formofball3.title: Form of the ballot question
amend48-gen-formofball3.plain: Each proposed amendment and law submitted to the people is described on the ballot by a description determined by the attorney-general, and the secretary of the commonwealth numbers each question and prints it in the set form, stating whether and by what vote the general court approved it.

amend48-gen-infoforvote4.title: Information for voters on ballot measures
amend48-gen-infoforvote4.plain: Annulled: It required the secretary of the commonwealth to print and send each registered voter the full text of every measure submitted to the people, with committee reports, the general court's votes and the ballot description, and other information and arguments. Notes in the text say it was superseded.

amend48-gen-thevetopowe5.title: Veto power over amending laws approved by the people
amend48-gen-thevetopowe5.plain: The general court may amend or repeal a law approved by the people, subject to the veto power of the governor and to the right of referendum by petition.
powers: the general court may amend or repeal a law approved by the people

amend48-gen-thegenecour6.title: General court's power to repeal laws approved by the people
amend48-gen-thegenecour6.plain: The general court may amend or repeal a law approved by the people, subject to the veto power of the governor and to the right of referendum by petition.
powers: the general court may amend or repeal a law approved by the people

amend48-gen-amendeclto7.title: Initiative and referendum amendment is self-executing
amend48-gen-amendeclto7.plain: This article of amendment is self-executing, but legislation not inconsistent with it may be enacted to facilitate the operation of its provisions.
powers: legislation not inconsistent with anything herein contained may be enacted to facilitate the operation of its provisions

amend48-gen-artiixand8.title: Articles IX and XLII of amendments annulled
amend48-gen-artiixand8.plain: Article IX and Article XLII of the amendments of the constitution are annulled.

amend49.title: Conservation of natural resources
amend49.plain: Annulled: It declared the conservation, development and utilization of the commonwealth's natural resources public uses, and gave the general court power to provide for taking lands and interests, upon payment of just compensation, for that purpose. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art. XCVII.

amend50.title: Regulating advertising
amend50.plain: Advertising on public ways, in public places and on private property within public view may be regulated and restricted by law.
powers: may be regulated and restricted by law

amend51.title: Preserving historical landmarks
amend51.plain: Preserving ancient landmarks and other property of historical or antiquarian interest is a public use, and the commonwealth and its cities and towns may take such property, upon payment of just compensation, under regulations the general court prescribes.
powers: the commonwealth and the cities and towns therein may, upon payment of just compensation, take such property or any interest therein

amend52.title: Recesses of the general court
amend52.plain: Annulled: It let the general court, by concurrent vote of the two houses, take recesses amounting to not more than thirty days, none extending beyond the sixtieth day from their first assembling. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art. CII.

amend53.title: Appointing and removing military officers
amend53.plain: Annuls earlier provisions and adopts a new Article X: military and naval officers are selected, appointed and removed as the general court prescribes by law, but none is appointed without passing an examination or serving one year; the governor commissions officers entitled to commissions.
powers: may be removed in such manner as the general court may by law prescribe
limits: no such officer shall be appointed unless

amend54.title: Military and naval forces and the commander-in-chief
amend54.plain: Annuls an earlier article and adopts a new Article VII: the general court provides by law for the military and naval forces; the governor is commander-in-chief, may assemble and employ them, and may, as authorized by the general court, prescribe their organization and regulations.
powers: The governor shall be the commander-in-chief thereof
shall have power to assemble the whole or any part of them for training, instruction or parade
to employ them for the suppression of rebellion, the repelling of invasion, and the enforcement of the laws
prescribe from time to time the organization of the military and naval forces and make regulations for their government

amend55.title: Succession when governor and lieutenant-governor are vacant
amend55.plain: Annuls an earlier article and provides that when both the offices of governor and lieutenant-governor are vacant, the secretary, attorney-general, treasurer and receiver-general, and auditor, in that order, have full power to do what the governor or lieutenant-governor could lawfully do.
powers: have full power and authority to do and execute all and every such acts, matters and things as the governor or the lieutenant-governor might or could lawfully do or execute

amend56.title: Governor returning bills with recommended amendments
amend56.plain: Annulled: It gave the governor, within five days, the right to return a bill or resolve to its originating branch recommending amendments; if re-enacted in any form it went back to the governor, who could not return it a second time. A note says it was superseded.

amend57.title: Women eligible as notaries public
amend57.plain: Amends Article IV of the articles of amendment by adding that women shall be eligible to appointment as notaries public. The bracketed sentence on change of name voiding the commission is printed as superseded.
rights: Women shall be eligible to appointment as notaries public

amend58.title: Retiring officers for age or disability
amend58.plain: Annulled: It amended Article I of Chapter III of Part the Second to let the governor, with the consent of the council, after due notice and hearing, retire such officers because of advanced age or mental or physical disability. A note says it was superseded.

amend59.title: Charters subject to revocation and amendment
amend59.plain: Every charter, franchise or act of incorporation shall forever remain subject to revocation and amendment.
powers: shall forever remain subject to revocation and amendment

amend60.title: Limiting buildings to districts
amend60.plain: The general court has power to limit buildings, according to their use or construction, to specified districts of cities and towns.
powers: The general court shall have power to limit buildings according to their use or construction to specified districts of cities and towns

amend61.title: Compulsory voting and secret voting
amend61.plain: The general court has authority to provide for compulsory voting at elections, but the right of secret voting shall be preserved.
rights: the right of secret voting
powers: shall have authority to provide for compulsory voting at elections

amend62.title: Credit and borrowing of the commonwealth
amend62.plain: Annulled: It barred lending the commonwealth's credit to individuals, private associations or privately owned corporations; let it borrow to repel invasion, suppress insurrection, defend itself or assist the United States in war, or in anticipation of revenue; otherwise required a two-thirds vote; and limited use of borrowed money. A note says it was superseded.

amend63.title: Revenue, budget and appropriations
amend63.plain: Annulled: It required all money received to be paid into the treasury, a budget from the governor within three weeks, a single general appropriation bill, and special appropriation bills only as provided, and let the governor disapprove or reduce items. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CVII.

amend64.title: Biennial elections and terms of state officers
amend64.plain: Annulled: It provided for biennial election of the governor, other state officers, senators and representatives and set their terms, limited the treasurer to three successive terms, and had the general court assemble every year on the first Wednesday in January. Notes say it was annulled.

amend65.title: Legislators barred from new or better-paid offices
amend65.plain: No person elected to the general court may, during the term for which he was elected, be appointed to any office created or whose emoluments are increased during that term, nor receive extra pay for service on a recess committee or commission, except a statutes-revision committee.
limits: be appointed to any office created or the emoluments whereof are increased during such term
nor receive additional salary or compensation for service upon any recess committee or commission

amend66.title: Executive work organized in departments
amend66.plain: Annulled: It required the executive and administrative work of the commonwealth to be organized, by January first, 1921, in not more than twenty departments, under such supervision and regulation as the general court prescribes by law. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. LXXXVII.

amend67.title: Recorded vote on emergency preamble
amend67.plain: Amends Article XLVIII so that a separate recorded vote is taken on an emergency law's preamble, which must be adopted by two-thirds of the members of each House voting; on request of two senators or five representatives, that vote is by yeas and nays.
limits: unless the preamble is adopted by two-thirds of the members of each House voting thereon, the law shall not be an emergency law

amend68.title: Striking the word "male" from Article III
amend68.plain: Amends Article III of the amendments to the constitution, as amended, by striking out the word "male" in its first line.

amend69.title: Sex no bar to office; women re-registering after name change
amend69.plain: No person shall be deemed ineligible to hold state, county or municipal office by reason of sex. It also amends Article IV so that a woman who changes her name shall re-register under her new name and pay a fee set by the general court.
limits: No person shall be deemed to be ineligible to hold state, county or municipal office by reason of sex

amend70.title: Limited town meetings in larger towns
amend70.plain: Annulled: It added to Article II that the general court could establish, in towns of more than six thousand inhabitants, a town meeting limited to elected inhabitants, with the consent and on application of a majority of the inhabitants voting. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. LXXXIX.

amend71.title: Census and representative and senatorial districts
amend71.plain: Annulled: It replaced Articles XXI and XXII, providing a census and special enumeration of legal voters every ten years from 1935 as the basis for apportioning two hundred and forty representatives and forty senators into districts. A note says it was superseded.

amend72.title: Biennial sessions and biennial budget
amend72.plain: Annulled: It had the general court assemble in regular session biennially, made the budget cover two years, and annulled provisions requiring the general court to meet annually. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. LXXV.

amend73.title: Governor's power of pardoning
amend73.plain: Replaces an earlier article: the governor, with the advice of council, has the power of pardoning offences except impeachment convictions; for a felony the general court may prescribe pardon terms and conditions; a pardon granted before conviction shall not avail the party pleading it.
powers: The power of pardoning offences
shall be in the governor, by and with the advice of council
the general court shall have power to prescribe the terms and conditions upon which a pardon may be granted
limits: no charter of pardon, granted by the governor, with advice of the council before conviction, shall avail the party pleading the same

amend74.title: Initiative petitions, ballot summaries and voter information
amend74.plain: Amends Article XLVIII: initiative petitions are first signed by ten voters and certified by the attorney-general; petition blanks and ballots carry a fair, concise summary of each measure; and the secretary of the commonwealth sends voters the full text and information on every measure.
