amend75.title: Article LXXII on biennial sessions annulled
amend75.plain: Annuls Article LXXII, which provided for biennial sessions of the general court and a biennial budget; provisions annulled or affected by it shall have the same force and effect as though it had not been adopted.

amend76.title: Absentee voting
amend76.plain: Annulled: It replaced Article XLV, giving the general court power to provide by law for voting by qualified voters who at election time are absent from their city or town or unable by physical disability to vote in person. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art. CV.

amend77.title: Liberty of the press and free speech
amend77.plain: Replaces Article XVI of Part the First: the liberty of the press is essential to the security of freedom in a state and ought not to be restrained in this commonwealth, and the right of free speech shall not be abridged.
rights: The liberty of the press
The right of free speech
limits: it ought not, therefore, to be restrained in this commonwealth
shall not be abridged

amend78.title: Highway revenue used only for highways
amend78.plain: Annulled: It barred spending revenue from vehicle registration, operation or use, or from motor fuels, for anything other than listed highway purposes, to be spent as the general court directs, except an excise in lieu of local property taxes. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CIV.

amend79.title: Filling vacancies in state offices from the people at large
amend79.plain: Amends Article XVII so that, if an officer is not elected in November or the person elected dies, the senators and representatives choose by joint ballot from the people at large; vacancies arising outside a session are filled by the governor with the council's advice and consent.

amend80.title: Revised terms of state officers
amend80.plain: Annulled: It replaced Section 1 of Article LXIV, keeping biennial elections, starting the governor's, lieutenant-governor's and councillors' terms at noon on a Thursday in January, and providing for deaths of the governor elect and lieutenant-governor elect. A note says it was annulled and superseded.

amend81.title: Initiative and referendum signature thresholds
amend81.plain: Amends Article XLVIII: initiative and referendum petitions need signatures equal to set percentages of the vote cast for governor; it revises joint sessions on proposed amendments, legislative action on initiative laws, amendment by petitioners, and changes thirty days to sixty days before submission.

amend82.title: Four-year terms for governor and state officers
amend82.plain: Replaces Article LXIV: the governor, lieutenant-governor, secretary, treasurer and receiver-general, attorney general and auditor are elected quadrennially, and councillors, senators and representatives biennially; it sets their terms, and the general court assembles every year on the first Wednesday in January.

amend83.title: Continuity of government in emergencies
amend83.plain: The general court has full power to provide for prompt and temporary succession to public offices whose incumbents become unavailable in emergencies resulting from disaster caused by enemy attack, and to adopt measures necessary and proper for continuity of government of the commonwealth and its political subdivisions.
powers: The general court shall have full power and authority to provide for prompt and temporary succession to the powers and duties of public offices
to adopt such other measures as may be necessary and proper for insuring continuity of the government of the commonwealth and the governments of its political subdivisions

amend84.title: Giving or lending the commonwealth's credit
amend84.plain: Replaces Section 1 of Article LXII: the commonwealth may give, loan or pledge its credit only by a two-thirds yea-and-nay vote of each house of the general court, and its credit shall not be given or loaned to any individual, private association or privately owned and managed corporation.
powers: The commonwealth may give, loan or pledge its credit
limits: only by a vote, taken by the yeas and nays, of two-thirds of each house of the general court present and voting thereon
The credit of the commonwealth shall not in any manner be given or loaned to or in aid of any individual

amend85.title: Opinions of the justices
amend85.plain: Replaces Article II of Chapter III: each branch of the legislature, and the governor or the council, may require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court upon important questions of law and upon solemn occasions.
powers: shall have authority to require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court

amend86.title: Governor and lieutenant-governor voted on as a group
amend86.plain: Party candidates for governor and lieutenant-governor are grouped on the state election ballot by party; a voter may cast a single vote for a group, counting for each candidate in it, but may not vote for only one of them.
rights: the voter may cast a single vote for any such group
limits: may not cast a vote for only one of the candidates in such group

amend87.title: Governor's executive reorganization plans
amend87.plain: The governor may present reorganization plans for executive agencies to the general court; a committee holds a hearing and reports, and a plan has the force of law after sixty days unless disapproved by a majority of either branch. Plans cannot be amended during those sixty days.
powers: the governor may prepare one or more reorganization plans
such reorganization plan shall have the force of law upon expiration of the sixty calendar days next following its presentation by the governor to the general court
limits: no such reorganization plan shall be subject to amendment by the general court before expiration of such sixty days

amend88.title: Industrial development of cities and towns
amend88.plain: The industrial development of cities and towns is a public function, and the commonwealth and its cities and towns may provide for it in the manner the general court determines.
powers: the commonwealth and the cities and towns therein may provide for the same

amend89.title: Home rule for cities and towns
amend89.plain: Replaces Article II: grants the people of every city and town the right of self-government in local matters, sets how charters are adopted, revised and amended, lists powers not granted, and limits the general court to general laws or listed special laws. The bracketed words "ten months" were superseded.
rights: the right of self-government in local matters
powers: Any city or town shall have the power to adopt or revise a charter or to amend its existing charter
exercise any power or function which the general court has power to confer upon it
The general court shall have the power to act in relation to cities and towns
limits: No town of fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants shall adopt a city form of government
Nothing in this article shall be deemed to grant to any city or town the power to
but only by general laws which apply alike to all cities or to all towns, or to all cities and towns, or to a class of not fewer than two

amend90.title: Governor's ten days to act on bills
amend90.plain: Amends four articles to give the governor ten days: an unreturned bill or resolve becomes law; a pocket veto applies if the general court adjourns within ten days; the governor may return a bill recommending amendment once; and item vetoes or reductions in appropriation bills must be explained within ten days.
powers: shall have the right to return it to the branch of the general court in which it originated with a recommendation that any amendment or amendments specified by him be made therein
The governor may disapprove or reduce items or parts of items in any bill appropriating money
limits: he shall have no right to return the same a second time with a recommendation to amend

amend91.title: Governor's inability and vacancy
amend91.plain: The office of governor is deemed vacant when the governor, or the chief justice and a majority of the associate justices (or another body the general court provides), declares in writing that the governor is unable to discharge the office; it sets how the governor resumes, how the general court decides disputes, and when a special election is held.
powers: Thereupon the general court shall decide the issue

amend92.title: Census and 240 representative districts
amend92.plain: Annulled: It provided a census every tenth year from 1971 as the basis for two hundred and forty representative districts and forty senatorial and councillor districts, and annulled Articles XXI and XXII as appearing in Article LXXI. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CI.

amend93.title: Striking a one-year residence requirement
amend93.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the words "within the commonwealth one year, and".

amend94.title: Changing "twenty-one" to "nineteen" in Article III
amend94.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the word "twenty-one" and inserting in its place the word "nineteen".

amend95.title: Striking "pauper and" from Article III
amend95.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the words "pauper and".

amend96.title: State loans for higher education
amend96.plain: The general court has power to authorize the commonwealth to make loans, on terms it deems reasonable, to residents of the commonwealth for tuition and board at any college, university or other institution of higher learning.
powers: The general court shall have power to authorize the commonwealth to make loans

amend97.title: Right to clean air, water and environment
amend97.plain: Replaces Article XLIX: the people have the right to clean air and water, freedom from excessive noise, and the natural, scenic, historic and esthetic qualities of their environment; the general court may protect these rights and take lands, which may be put to other uses only by a two-thirds vote.
rights: The people shall have the right to clean air and water, freedom from excessive and unnecessary noise, and the natural, scenic, historic, and esthetic qualities of their environment
powers: The general court shall have the power to enact legislation necessary or expedient to protect such rights
the general court shall have the power to provide for the taking, upon payment of just compensation therefor
limits: shall not be used for other purposes or otherwise disposed of except by laws enacted by a two thirds vote

amend98.title: Tenure and retirement of judges
amend98.plain: Replaces Article I of Chapter III: judicial officers hold office during good behavior; the governor, with the council's consent, may remove them on address of both houses or retire them for advanced age or disability after notice and hearing; judges shall be retired at seventy.
powers: the governor, with the consent of the council, may remove them upon the address of both houses of the legislature
the governor, with the consent of the council, may after due notice and hearing retire them

amend99.title: Taxing farm land by its agricultural use
amend99.plain: The general court may prescribe that agricultural or horticultural lands be valued for taxation by their agricultural or horticultural uses, but no parcel under five acres, or not actively so used for the two preceding years, shall be valued at less than fair market value.
powers: Full power and authority are hereby given and granted to the general court to prescribe
limits: shall be valued at less than fair market value under this article

amend100.title: Voting age changed to eighteen
amend100.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the word giving the age at which a citizen has a right to vote for Governor and other public officers and inserting the word "eighteen".

amend101.title: 160 representative districts and 40 senate districts
amend101.plain: The house has one hundred and sixty members and the senate forty, in districts of contiguous territory with equal numbers of inhabitants as nearly as may be; voters may petition the supreme judicial court about districts, and Article XCII is annulled. Bracketed census wording was superseded.
powers: Original jurisdiction is hereby vested in the supreme judicial court
The General Court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted
limits: no town containing less than twenty-five hundred inhabitants according to said census shall be divided

amend102.title: Legislative recesses
amend102.plain: Replaces Article LII: the General Court, by concurrent vote of the two houses, may take a recess or recesses amounting to not more than thirty days.
powers: may take a recess or recesses
limits: amounting to not more than thirty days

amend103.title: No public money for private or religious institutions
amend103.plain: Replaces Section 2 of Article XLVI: no public money, property or credit may aid any institution, school or undertaking not publicly owned and controlled, or any church or religious society, with listed exceptions; grants-in-aid to private higher educational institutions or their students are allowed.
limits: No grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of credit shall be made or authorized

no such grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of public credit shall be made or authorized for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any church, religious denomination or society

amend104.title: Highway revenue only for highways and mass transportation
amend104.plain: Replaces Article LXXVIII: revenue from vehicle fees, duties, excises or license taxes and from vehicle fuels shall be spent only for listed highway and mass transportation purposes, except revenue from an excise tax imposed in lieu of local property taxes.
limits: shall be expended for other than cost of administration of laws providing for such revenue
shall be expended by the commonwealth or its counties, cities and towns for said highway and mass transportation purposes only

amend105.title: Absentee voting
amend105.plain: Replaces Article XLV: the general court may provide by law for voting by qualified voters who at the time of an election are absent from their city or town, unable by physical disability to vote in person at the polling places, or hold religious beliefs in conflict with voting that day.
powers: The general court shall have power to provide by law for voting

amend106.title: Natural rights and equality under the law
amend106.plain: Replaces Article I of Part the First: all people are born free and equal with natural, essential and unalienable rights, including life, liberty, property, safety and happiness; equality under the law shall not be denied or abridged because of sex, race, color, creed or national origin.
rights: All people are born free and equal
the right of enjoying and defending their lives and liberties
that of acquiring, possessing and protecting property
that of seeking and obtaining their safety and happiness
Equality under the law
limits: shall not be denied or abridged because of sex, race, color, creed or national origin

amend107.title: The governor's budget
amend107.plain: Replaces Section 2 of Article LXIII: within three weeks after the general court convenes (eight weeks in a new governor's first year), the governor shall recommend a budget of all proposed expenditures and the means to pay them, and may require information from any board, commission, officer or department.
powers: the governor shall have the power to require any board, commission, officer or department to furnish him with any information

amend108.title: Information for voters on ballot measures
amend108.plain: Replaces subheading IV of Article XLVIII: the secretary of the commonwealth shall print and send to each eligible voter or residence the full text of every measure, committee reports, the general court's votes and a ballot summary, and other information and arguments as provided by law.

amend109.title: Who counts as an inhabitant in the census
amend109.plain: Amends the first paragraph of Section 1 of Article CI: for the census, every person is an inhabitant of the city or town of his usual place of residence under federal census standards, subject to exceptions the general court may provide, and the census shall specify inhabitants of each precinct and ward.

amend110.title: Taxing forest, wildlife and recreational lands
amend110.plain: Replaces Article XLI: the general court has full power to prescribe methods of taxation for wild or forest lands kept natural for wildlife and natural resources, and for recreational lands, that will develop and conserve those resources and benefits.
powers: Full power and authority are hereby given and granted to the general court to prescribe

amend111.title: No school assignment by race
amend111.plain: No student shall be assigned to or denied admittance to a public school on the basis of race, color, national origin or creed.
limits: No student shall be assigned to or denied admittance to a public school on the basis of race, color, national origin or creed

amend112.title: Classifying real property for taxes
amend112.plain: Amends Article IV of Chapter I of Part the Second: the general court may classify real property by use in no more than four classes and tax the classes differently, but proportionately within a class, and reasonable exemptions may be granted.

amend113.title: Changing "ten months" to "eighteen months"
amend113.plain: Amends the first sentence of the sixth paragraph of Section 3 of Article II of the Amendments, as appearing in Article LXXXIX, by striking out the words "ten months" and inserting the words "eighteen months".

amend114.title: No discrimination against handicapped individuals
amend114.plain: No otherwise qualified handicapped individual shall, solely by reason of his handicap, be excluded from, denied the benefits of, or be subject to discrimination under any program or activity within the commonwealth.
limits: be excluded from the participation in, denied the benefits of, or be subject to discrimination under any program or activity within the commonwealth

amend115.title: State-mandated costs of municipal employment
amend115.plain: A law imposing additional costs on two or more cities or towns by regulating municipal employment is not effective in a city or town until accepted there, unless enacted by a two-thirds vote of each house or the general court provides for the commonwealth to assume the cost.
limits: shall be effective in any city or town until such law is accepted

amend116.title: Punishment of death
amend116.plain: Adds two sentences to Article XXVI of Part the First: no provision of the Constitution shall be construed as prohibiting the punishment of death, and the general court may authorize its imposition by courts having jurisdiction of crimes subject to it.

amend117.title: Census as basis for districts
amend117.plain: Amends Sections 1 and 2 of Article CI so that the federal census is the basis for representative, senatorial and councillor districts for the ten year period from the first Wednesday in a set January after the census. The bracketed word "fifth" was superseded; notes say both sections were amended by Article CXIX.

amend118.title: Pay of members of the general court
amend118.plain: The base compensation of members of the general court as of January 1, 1996 shall not be changed except as this article provides: from January 2001 and every second year, it rises or falls at the same rate as the commonwealth's median household income, as ascertained by the governor.
limits: shall not be changed except as provided in this article

amend119.title: Census districts begin the third January
amend119.plain: Amends Sections 1 and 2 of Article CI, as appearing in Article CXVII: the federal census is the basis for representative, senatorial and councillor districts for the ten year period beginning with the first Wednesday in the third January following the census.

amend120.title: Excluding incarcerated felons from voting
amend120.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by inserting after the word "upwards" the words "excepting persons who are incarcerated in a correctional facility due to a felony conviction, and".

amend121.title: Additional income tax on income over $1,000,000
amend121.plain: Adds a paragraph to Article XLIV: an additional 4 percent tax applies to annual taxable income over $1,000,000, adjusted yearly for cost of living, and its revenues shall be spent, subject to appropriation, only for public education, public colleges and universities, and roads, bridges and public transportation.
limits: shall be expended, subject to appropriation, only for these purposes
